situation.text: PST expects Russian intelligence to attempt sabotage in Norway within the next year, most likely against defence firms, their suppliers and military logistics. Forsvaret has cancelled Valiant Defender, a large allied exercise planned for March 2027, to put resources into Joint Viking in Indre Troms, the Heimdall autonomy trial and NATO's Formidable Shield at Andøya. Germany says Norway and Germany will jointly fund a new air defence package for Ukraine through NATO's PURL scheme.

Estonia's security service says Russia is preparing sabotage against about ten Estonian defence companies, and the Baltic states received the same warning as Poland about a Russian plot near Kaliningrad. Latvia showed its first naval drones at its Independence Day parade. Finland and Ukraine agreed to produce weapons together in Finland, while Swedish founders complain that the fast-track procurement route is closed to small firms.

Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge for the third time in a week overnight into 19 November, and rail traffic has stopped after the road section already collapsed. Russia launched 98 drones the same night and Ukraine says it downed 69, while strikes on energy left 99 settlements in Mykolaiv region without power. The European Commission proposes a new EUR 45 bn loan for 2027, of which EUR 25 bn is for military needs.

Polish media report that Poland foiled a Russian plot near the Kaliningrad border meant to cause mass casualties and be blamed on Ukraine. A Russian drone forced Moldova to close its airspace on 17 November. NATO has agreed to use OpenAI's tools for cyber defence, and Germany ordered four more MEKO frigates from TKMS.

news.title: Forsvaret cancels the big Valiant Defender exercise planned for 2027
news.summary: The Chief of Defence has dropped Valiant Defender, a large allied exercise planned for March 2027, possibly in Finnmark and Indre Troms, citing changed strategic priorities. Resources go instead to Heimdall in February, a trial of autonomous systems in Arctic conditions, and NATO's Formidable Shield missile exercise at Andøya in April. Joint Viking will be held in Indre Troms in March with about 4,000 troops, and Cold Response 2028 is planned to be larger. Heimdall is the 2027 test window to watch for autonomy startups.

news.title: Norway and Germany to fund a new air defence package for Ukraine
news.summary: German defence minister Boris Pistorius announced at the Ramstein meeting in Brussels that Norway and Germany will jointly pay for a package of mainly air defence through NATO's PURL scheme, which buys US-made equipment for Ukraine. No amount was given, and NTB could not get the Norwegian government to confirm it. Most PURL money goes to US suppliers, not Norwegian industry.

news.title: MPs want security review of Russian-linked bid for Arctic copper mine
news.summary: Artem Volynets, a former close associate of sanctioned oligarch Oleg Deripaska, is trying to buy the Nussir copper mine near Hammerfest through ACG Metals, and also a mine in Sulitjelma. Several MPs say the deal could threaten national security and want it stopped. A Green Party proposal to pause it until security services clear it did not get enough support. Ownership of critical minerals and sites in the north is becoming a security question.

news.title: Norway and the UK agree to work closer on AI
news.summary: Norway's digitalisation minister and the UK's AI minister met aboard HMS Prince of Wales in Oslo. They agreed on cooperation on responsible AI, countering AI-driven cyber threats and keeping control of advanced AI systems. It is part of the two countries' strategic partnership.

news.title: Syncrolift wins NOK 940 m contract for world's largest shiplift at a US naval yard
news.summary: The Norwegian firm, part of Nekkar, calls it the largest contract in its history. It more than doubles its order backlog. Norwegian maritime suppliers are finding a way into the US naval build-up.

news.title: Norway turns its Ukraine industry portal into a marketplace
news.summary: The defence ministry's portal for Norwegian offers to Ukraine no longer has earmarked Nansen money. Proposals are now matched to needs that Ukraine's defence ministry confirms, and FMA assesses those that match. Unused funds move into the ordinary Ukraine support budget.

news.title: Norwegian Robot Aviation builds Arctic-ready drones for Norway's military
news.summary: The company has grown from five to almost 60 staff since 2023. It aims to be as independent of foreign suppliers as possible and says its finances are sound. A Norwegian example of the supply-chain independence buyers now ask for.

news.title: PST raises sabotage threat in Norway
news.summary: PST expects Russian intelligence to attempt sabotage in Norway in the coming year, often through hired proxies. The defence industry, defence-related firms and their suppliers, such as logistics companies, are the most likely targets. Methods include arson, explosives and drones. Every defence startup should review site security and report anything unusual to PST.

news.title: Business Finland doubled its defence funding
news.summary: Finnish companies received about EUR 75 m in defence and security funding from Business Finland in 2025, double the year before. The money runs through its Defense and Digital Resilience programme, and a new two-year growth project starts in January. Finland's state innovation agency is now a serious funder of defence startups, a benchmark for Innovasjon Norge.

news.title: Founders say Sweden's defence fast track is closed to small companies
news.summary: The CEO of Polar Mist says FMV's fast-track procurement is open to only a few players, according to Dagens industri. Stark Defence's Nordic chairman says foreign firms can wait months to set up in Sweden. A fast track that only primes can use limits the gain for startups.

news.title: Latvia shows its first naval drones
news.summary: Four uncrewed surface vessels from Latvian firm NEWT21 appeared at the Independence Day parade in Riga. FOG is a fast craft for reconnaissance, interception and strike; RAY is a catamaran for logistics, reconnaissance and evacuation. Baltic states are building their own maritime drone capacity.

news.title: Navantia courts Danish suppliers in the frigate race
news.summary: Spanish shipbuilder Navantia expects to sign agreements with Danish companies within about a month as part of its F110 bid for Denmark's new frigates. It competes with Babcock and Naval Group, which has already signed with three Danish partners. Bidders are shopping for local partners now, a chance for Nordic subsuppliers.

news.title: Finland and Ukraine agree to make weapons together in Finland
news.summary: The two defence ministers signed a memorandum at the Ramstein meeting in Brussels. It covers technology transfer, new production sites in Finland and joint development of new systems. No products, companies or amounts were named.

news.title: Teracom buys Sweden's national drone test site
news.summary: The state-owned secure network operator has bought Västervik Drone Science Park, home to Sweden's first and largest zone for unmanned aircraft. Teracom wants to make it a national and international hub for testing drones, with its own know-how in resilient connectivity, control and data links. It is also in talks to buy the local airport area.

news.title: Iceye bids about EUR 2 bn for Italian rocket maker Avio
news.summary: The Finnish radar-satellite company offers EUR 41 per share in cash for Avio, maker of the Vega rocket, and promises EUR 1 bn of further investment in Italy over five years. Iceye wants to build a vertically integrated European space and defence group with its own launch capacity. The offer needs regulatory approval.

news.title: Kelluu turns its airships into passive radars
news.summary: The Finnish firm unveiled Halo, a passive radar built into its airship hulls that tracks targets using reflected radio, TV and mobile signals and never transmits. Kelluu says it can more than double the range of ground-based passive radars at far lower hourly cost than crewed radar aircraft. A closed pilot with five partner nations is planned for early 2027.

news.title: Third strike on the Kerch bridge halts rail traffic
news.summary: Ukraine hit the railway section of the bridge overnight into 19 November, after strikes on 16 and 17 November brought down an arch and part of the road. Russian-installed authorities in Crimea say train traffic has stopped. Ukraine's defence ministry says the bridge no longer works as a transport route.

news.title: EU proposes a new EUR 45 bn loan for Ukraine in 2027
news.summary: The European Commission proposes EUR 25 bn for military needs and EUR 20 bn for budget support, on top of the EUR 90 bn Ukraine Support Loan. Ukraine would repay only after receiving Russian reparations. EU leaders discuss it at a summit on 26–27 November. More EU money for Ukrainian procurement means more demand for drones and air defence next year.

news.title: Russia reportedly tests a Geran-6 jet drone at up to 1,000 km/h
news.summary: A member of the Ukrainian parliament's security committee says intelligence shows Russia testing the Geran-6, a small cruise missile with a large warhead. The claim is not independently confirmed. Faster one-way attack drones raise the bar for detection and interceptors.

news.title: UK sends over 1,000 air defence missiles and a dozen radars
news.summary: The GBP 240 m package, part of GBP 500 m set aside in the UK budget, covers short-range air defence missiles that have worked well against jet-powered Shaheds, plus more than a dozen radars. Deliveries start in mid-December to close gaps this winter.

news.title: Bundeswehr tests Ukraine's DELTA battle management system
news.summary: Germany's defence minister said the German Army tested DELTA, Ukraine's digital situational awareness system, during drone exercises last month with help from Ukrainian instructors. Germany wants to develop it further with Ukraine and test it in the Bundeswehr. Ukrainian software is starting to flow back into European armies.

news.title: Destinus says its Ruta missiles brought down the Kerch bridge span
news.summary: The European company says Ruta missiles hit the bridge on two days running, and that seven more missiles caused a span to collapse. Its Lord long-range drones, called Da Vinci in Ukraine, were used to suppress Russian air defence. The claims come from the company and are not independently confirmed.

news.title: Kerch bridge arch collapses after second Ukrainian strike
news.summary: Ukraine hit the bridge between Crimea and Russia on 16 November and again overnight into 17 November. The arch over the shipping channel and an adjacent road section fell into the water and traffic has stopped. Ukraine has struck at least six bridges on Russia's key logistics routes since early October.

news.title: Half of Russia's overnight attack drones were jet-powered
news.summary: Russia launched 158 drones from 18:00 on 15 November, including 77 jet-powered Shaheds, Gerbera drones and decoys. Ukraine says it shot down or jammed 131, with hits at 19 locations. Faster jet drones push counter-drone systems toward quicker sensors and interceptors.

news.title: NATO signs cyber defence deal with OpenAI
news.summary: Announced at the NATO Edge conference in Izmir, the deal gives NATO access to OpenAI's Daybreak security platform to review software, fix weak points and examine suspicious activity. OpenAI already supported NATO's Crossed Swords exercise in Tallinn, where operators tested AI agents for cyber defence. Big AI firms are moving into defence cyber, which raises the bar for small cyber startups.

news.title: Poland foils Russian plot meant to kill many and blame Ukraine
news.summary: Rzeczpospolita reports that Polish intelligence and the military stopped a Russian sabotage plan near the Kaliningrad border, after a warning from foreign services. Police, ABW officers and special forces were sent to the area, and Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia got similar warnings. Hybrid attacks are escalating from sabotage toward mass-casualty plots.

news.title: KNDS unveils FENNEK AIR counter-drone vehicle
news.summary: KNDS Deutschland will show a FENNEK AIR prototype at NEDS in Rotterdam, with a 30 mm cannon and AI that detects, tracks and prioritises drones. The vehicles share sensor data over a network, and the kit could fit other platforms. Primes are bundling AI targeting into mobile air defence, where software and sensor startups can partner.

news.title: Germany puts IRIS-T missiles into NASAMS for Ukraine
news.summary: Germany's defence minister says IRIS-T missiles are being integrated into the NASAMS systems supplied to Ukraine, which today fire US AIM-9X and AMRAAM missiles. It is framed as a step to cut reliance on US weapons, and could widen export options for NASAMS, which Kongsberg makes with RTX.

news.title: Google: Russian-speaking hackers ran the first fully automated AI cyberattack
news.summary: Google says AI agents compared code before and after security updates, found flaws and built exploits with no human in the loop, hitting French media, entertainment and education websites. Google expects these tools to be used against organisations worldwide. Small defence firms are exposed targets and need to patch fast.

news.title: Moldova closes its airspace as a Russian drone heads for Chisinau
news.summary: A Geran-2 attack drone entered Moldovan airspace twice from Ukraine's Odesa region, and authorities closed the whole airspace. The foreign minister called it a serious violation of sovereignty. Drone spillover into neighbouring countries keeps widening demand for cheap detection.

news.title: Belgium orders radars and Skyranger air defence
news.summary: As part of its Blue Dome programme, Belgium ordered 14 Thales Ground Master 200 radars and 20 Rheinmetall Skyranger 30 short-range air defence systems, a contract worth several hundred million euros. Short-range air defence against drones is now standard on European shopping lists.

news.title: Romania fines Rheinmetall for late air defence deliveries
news.summary: Romania's defence minister says a first EUR 8.7 m penalty was invoiced on 8 November, apparently over a 2023 contract to upgrade Oerlikon guns to Skynex. More penalties may follow if the systems miss specifications. Delays by primes open doors for faster suppliers.

press.title: Atlantic Future Forum 2026: co-hosts' statement
press.summary: Representatives of 29 countries met in Oslo on 11–12 November aboard HMS Prince of Wales, at the invitation of the UK and Norway. They affirmed NATO as the base of collective security and welcomed greater European leadership in deterrence and defence. They noted the Northern Navies Framework signed by Joint Expeditionary Force naval chiefs on 10 November. The statement backs continued support for Ukraine and whole-of-society resilience. It calls for more production, faster technological innovation and a stronger European defence industrial base, including start-ups and SMEs alongside established primes.
press.startup: A political signal, not a programme: no money or procurement is attached. It gives startups a quotable line when they ask Norwegian and British buyers for a place next to the primes (inference).
press.tldr: Norway and the UK say start-ups belong next to the primes; hold them to it.

press.title: The industry portal for Ukraine has changed
press.summary: The portal, set up in November 2024 for Norwegian offers of technology and materiel to Ukraine, is now a marketplace showing defence capacities and opportunities. Ukraine's defence ministry should as a rule verify that a product matches a Ukrainian need. The portal no longer gets annual earmarked Nansen funds; unused money moves to the ordinary military support budget. FMA assesses the commercial, technical and legal side of proposals that match confirmed needs, and Forsvaret decides based on Ukrainian priorities and the budget. A ministry review found the old setup lacked clear rules for handling cases.
press.startup: Registering an offer no longer means a funded project; buys happen only when Ukraine confirms a concrete need. Startups should register and also build direct contact with Ukrainian units and Brave1 to get needs confirmed (inference).
press.tldr: Register on the portal, but get Ukraine to confirm the need first.

press.title: Work begins on a Nordic defence agreement
press.summary: Norway, Denmark, Finland, Sweden and Iceland will start work on a Nordic defence agreement, agreed at the NORDEFCO ministers' meeting in Oslo on 11–12 November. The goal is closer cooperation that strengthens NATO deterrence and lets Nordic forces operate seamlessly across borders. Ministers discussed a legal and political framework for peace, crisis and war, and want to remove practical and legal obstacles to moving forces. The Nordic countries together have about 250 modern fighter jets, 145 surface vessels and 100,000 personnel in peacetime. No timeline was given.
press.startup: The release does not mention procurement, but common rules for moving forces point toward more shared exercises, logistics and systems (inference). Products that work across all Nordic forces will have a bigger market.
press.tldr: Nordic forces are integrating; sell to all five, not one.

press.title: MoD asks agencies to prepare corrective actions after audit
press.summary: Riksrevisjonen found that the 2025 accounts of Forsvaret, FFI and FMA may contain material errors, and could not give an opinion on Forsvarsbygg. The MoD has ordered concrete action plans with reporting requirements. Forsvaret must strengthen inventory control with an annual stock-count plan, FMA risks booking purchases in the wrong fiscal year, and Forsvarsbygg gets an external review of its financial management.
press.startup: Expect stricter documentation on deliveries, invoice timing and inventory traceability when you sell to FMA or Forsvaret. There may be demand for inventory, traceability and financial-control tools.
press.tldr: Expect stricter paperwork when you deliver to FMA and Forsvaret.

press.title: Forsvaret modernises its emergency-network radios
press.summary: Forsvaret will buy 1,320 new terminals for Nødnett, the radio network shared with police, fire and health services. About 650 replace first-generation equipment; the Army gets 280 and the Home Guard 290. The new handheld Motorola MXP600 replaces the MT P850S, delivered through TC Connect and funded through the Defence Staff's ICT portfolio. Forsvaret says it needs several ways to communicate, including robust ground systems alongside satellite and broadband, and that the upgrade also eases cooperation with Nordic emergency services.
press.startup: The contract is already placed, so there is nothing to bid on. It shows Forsvaret values redundant communications and civil-military interoperability in total defence, a theme comms and C2 startups can pitch to (inference).
press.tldr: No tender, but Forsvaret wants redundant comms that work with civilian services.

press.title: Nordic defence ministers' meeting in Oslo
press.summary: Norway chairs NORDEFCO in 2026 and hosts the Nordic defence ministers in Oslo on 11–12 November. Topics include stronger Nordic defence cooperation within NATO and total defence. A press briefing is held on 12 November.
press.startup: Nordic joint procurement and shared test arenas are growing. A product that fits several Nordic forces is easier to scale than one built for Norway only.
press.tldr: Build for all the Nordic forces, not Norway alone.

press.titleNo: Norge har mottatt det første amfibiske bro- og fergesystemet M3N til Hæren
press.title: First M3N amphibious bridge and ferry system delivered to the Army
press.summary: FMA delivered the first M3N amphibious bridging and ferry system to the Army, giving better mobility across rivers and fjords.
press.startup: Limited direct relevance. Shows the Army's focus on mobility and logistics, where autonomy and maintenance tools can add value.
press.tldr: Low direct relevance; shows focus on Army mobility.

press.titleNo: Forsvarsmateriell inviterer norske verft til konkurranse om nye fartøy til Sjøforsvaret
press.title: Norwegian yards invited to compete for new Navy vessels
press.summary: National prequalification for up to 28 standardized vessels for the Navy, Coast Guard and allies: up to 10 ocean-going and 18 coastal. Split into two contracts to widen Norwegian participation. Vessels must be built in Norway; hulls may be built abroad. Apply via Mercell (documents, timeline, deadline); the notice is also on Doffin. Only a limited number of qualified suppliers will be invited to bid. Contact: forsvarsmateriell@fma.no, +47 23 09 30 03.
press.startup: Startups will not build ships, but autonomy, sensors, C2 software, drone hangars and maintenance tech can ride along as subsuppliers. Talk to the yards that prequalify.
press.tldr: Big ship deal: get in as a subsupplier through the yards.

press.titleNo: Regjeringen styrker norske investeringer i Ukraina med 1 milliard kroner
press.title: NOK 1 bn to strengthen Norwegian investment in Ukraine
press.summary: A NOK 1 bn framework over three years, taken from the military part of the Nansen programme and placed under the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries. Investinor manages it by investing in Norwegian-based funds that back Ukrainian defence companies. Investinor picks the funds; the fund managers pick the companies. Direct co-investments may follow.
press.startup: Norwegian–Ukrainian joint ventures and Ukrainian partners of Norwegian startups may become investable through these funds. Talk to Investinor and Norwegian defence-tech fund managers early.
press.tldr: New NOK 1 bn fund route makes Norwegian–Ukrainian ventures easier to finance.

press.titleNo: Styrker evnen til å oppdage droner i Finnmark
press.title: Stronger drone detection in Finnmark
press.summary: The Armed Forces place air-surveillance sensors (NASAMS) in Kirkenes to detect and warn of drones in the border area. About 30 soldiers from the Garrison of Sør-Varanger will be stationed there through the year. The deployment is preventive. Police enforce drone rules and the Armed Forces assist on request.
press.startup: Clear demand signal for low-cost drone detection and early warning in Arctic conditions. No tender is attached, but this is a use case to pitch to the Home Guard, FFI and FMA.
press.tldr: Clear demand for cheap Arctic drone detection, but no tender yet.

press.title: New Operational Support Command (FOSK) from 1 January 2027
press.summary: FLO and the Armed Forces Medical Services merge into the Norwegian Armed Forces Operational Support Command (FOSK) on 1 January 2027. FOSK supports other units with resources from the defence sector and the wider total defence system.
press.startup: A new buyer organisation for logistics, maintenance and medical solutions. Map who owns what in FOSK before 2027.
press.tldr: A new logistics and medical buyer from January 2027.

press.titleNo: Forsvarsmateriell signaliserer konkurransemodell for standardiserte fartøy
press.title: Market signal: competition model for standardized vessels (P1118)
press.summary: Up to 20 ocean-going vessels planned for Norway, the UK and Lithuania, split into one contract for up to 14 naval vessels and one for up to 6 coast guard vessels. One bidder should not win both. Target: contracts in 2027 and first delivery in 2030. The signal is preliminary and may change.
press.startup: Market signals are FMA's early warning to industry. Read P1118 now if your product belongs on a ship; integration slots are decided early.
press.tldr: Contracts in 2027, first ships in 2030; integration slots are decided now.

readings.title: The “Battle of Norway”
readings.publisher: Sahaidachnyi Security Center, supported by Buntar Aerospace
readings.summary: Argues that the most likely attack on Norway is not a ground invasion of Finnmark but a 'Battle of Britain' in the drone era: mass drone and missile strikes, sea drones and sabotage against energy, subsea cables and logistics. It sees a threat window of 2027–2029, while most Norwegian programmes mature in 2029–2036. Biggest gaps: counter-drone and ballistic defence, sabotage detection at sea, tactical electronic warfare and manpower in Finnmark. Recommends a standing Ukraine–Norway capability partnership, starting with a Home Guard counter-drone shield.
readings.tldr: Norway's real gap is cheap mass defence against drones and sabotage, and Ukraine can help close it fast.

readings.title: Sabotage threat in Norway raised
readings.summary: PST's updated assessment says Russian intelligence will likely attempt sabotage in Norway in the coming year, mostly through proxies. The defence industry, defence-related businesses and their suppliers are the most likely targets, followed by critical infrastructure such as energy. PST asks companies to know their normal picture and report anything that deviates from it.
readings.tldr: Defence startups and their suppliers are now named sabotage targets; secure your sites.

readings.title: EU strategy for a rapidly changing Arctic
readings.summary: The EU's new Arctic strategy replaces the 2021 framework and puts security and resilience first. It plans a maritime security hub for sharing information and monitoring Arctic waters, more icebreaker capacity and protection of critical infrastructure such as a secure subsea cable to Greenland. Russia's military build-up and hybrid tactics in the north are the stated reason.
readings.tldr: EU money and attention are moving to Arctic surveillance and infrastructure protection.

readings.title: National Threat Assessment 2026
readings.summary: Russian and Chinese intelligence activity is expected to rise, with focus on military targets, Ukraine support, the High North and critical infrastructure. Essential context for anyone selling security or surveillance tech.
readings.tldr: Russian and Chinese spying in Norway is rising; expect stricter security demands on suppliers.

readings.title: Fokus 2026
readings.summary: The intelligence service's annual open assessment of the external threats to Norway, with Russia's military posture in the north at the centre.
readings.tldr: Russia's military power in the north remains the core threat to Norway.

readings.title: Defence Expenditure of NATO Countries (2014–2026)
readings.summary: Official spending, share of GDP, equipment share and personnel for all allies. The numbers on the map above come from here.
readings.tldr: Every ally but Slovenia now spends 2%+ of GDP; the money is there.

readings.title: Forsvarsløftet: long-term plan for the defence sector 2025–2036
readings.summary: The cross-party plan behind about NOK 600 bn in extra defence spending over 12 years. Tells you what Norway will buy and when.
readings.tldr: NOK 600 bn extra over 12 years: this is Norway's shopping list.

readings.title: Meld. St. 33 (2024–2025): status of the long-term plan
readings.summary: Progress, challenges and risks in delivering the long-term plan. Useful to see where programmes are late and where faster solutions are needed.
readings.tldr: Several programmes are late; that is where faster solutions are welcome.

readings.title: Roadmap for increased production capacity in the defence industry
readings.summary: The government's roadmap for scaling Norwegian defence production. Relevant for manufacturers and suppliers to the primes.
readings.tldr: Norway wants more production at home; manufacturers and subsuppliers benefit.

readings.title: New law on defence and security procurement (report)
readings.summary: Proposal for a new procurement law for defence and security. Shapes how startups can be bought from in the future.
readings.tldr: Procurement rules are being rewritten; watch how they treat small firms.

readings.title: National Security Strategy
readings.summary: Norway's first national security strategy, tying together defence, total defence, economy and technology.
readings.tldr: Security now spans defence, economy and technology, which widens the dual-use market.

readings.title: Readiness Roadmap 2030
readings.summary: The EU's four flagships, including the European Drone Defence Initiative and Eastern Flank Watch, with milestones to 2030.
readings.tldr: The EU wants a working drone shield and eastern flank watch by 2027–2030.

readings.title: White Paper for European Defence – Readiness 2030
readings.summary: The ReArm Europe plan, up to EUR 800 bn, and the SAFE loan instrument. Explains where EU defence money flows.
readings.tldr: Up to EUR 800 bn in EU defence money; SAFE loans favour European suppliers.

readings.title: Defence spending: who is doing what? (July 2026)
readings.summary: Country-by-country analysis of NATO's 2026 figures and the path to the Hague 3.5% + 1.5% target.
readings.tldr: Spending is rising everywhere, fastest on the eastern flank and in the Nordics.

readings.title: Russia's hybrid warfare campaign in Europe
readings.summary: Briefing on sabotage, cyberattacks, disinformation and drone incursions across Europe.
readings.tldr: Sabotage and drone incursions are the new normal, creating demand for protection of critical infrastructure.

readings.title: Ukraine Support Tracker
readings.summary: Tracks military, financial and humanitarian aid to Ukraine by country.
readings.tldr: Shows who funds Ukraine and how much, so you can see where the money is.

funding.amount: Up to NOK 500k per application (depends on role)
funding.who: Norwegian actors with a formal role in an EU or EDF application
funding.tldr: Get paid to write your EDF bid. Apply at least four weeks before the EU deadline.

funding.title: Centres for defence capability, security and preparedness
funding.amount: Up to NOK 450 m for 5–9 centres
funding.who: Only applicants who sent a sketch by 5 June 2026
funding.tldr: Main call moved to early 2027. Join a centre consortium if you missed the sketch.

funding.title: NOK 1 bn Ukraine defence investment scheme
funding.amount: Fund investments, NOK 1 bn over 3 years
funding.who: Norwegian-based funds investing in Ukrainian defence companies
funding.tldr: Proposed November 2026. Norwegian–Ukrainian ventures should talk to fund managers now.

funding.title: Brave International
funding.who: Ukrainian and foreign companies; products tested in Ukraine
funding.tldr: Foreign firms can now win Brave1 grants. First joint calls not yet dated.

funding.title: Brave Norway
funding.who: Ukrainian and Norwegian defence startups (drones, AI)
funding.tldr: The Norway–Ukraine startup programme. Watch FFI and Brave1 for the next call.

funding.title: NATO DIANA challenge programme
funding.tldr: 2027 call closed 3 July 2026. Prepare now for the next call, usually mid-year.

funding.title: European Defence Fund (EDF) 2026 calls
funding.who: EU and EEA companies, Norway included
funding.tldr: 2026 calls closed 29 September. The 2027 work programme comes next.

funding.title: LINC: Launchpad for Innovative Norwegian Companies
funding.tldr: 2026 intake closed 20 April. Expect the next round in spring 2027.

tenders.title: Dynamic purchasing system: drone systems (RPAS)

tenders.title: Dynamic purchasing system: ship technology services

tenders.title: P1118 standardized vessels: prequalification
tenders.tldr: Yards bid; autonomy, sensor and C2 startups should team up with them now.

tenders.title: Digital learning platform for the defence sector (incl. AI content)

tenders.title: Laboratory services for the Norwegian defence

tenders.title: Procurement advisory to FMA

tenders.title: Operation of Forsvaret's unclassified internet services
tenders.tldr: Hosting and operations incl. Azure. For IT and cloud operators.

tenders.title: Dynamic purchasing system: software licences
tenders.tldr: Software vendors and resellers can qualify any time to sell licences and subscriptions to the defence sector.
